ety.text: From ice + -y; cf. Old English īsiġ.

senses.d: Pertaining to, resembling, or abounding in ice; cold; frosty.
Covered with ice, wholly or partially.
ex: Antarctica is the coldest, iciest place on Earth, which makes the recent warming event particularly worrying for many scientists.
Morning commuters in parts of Texas, Oklahoma and Arkansas discovered slick sidewalks and icy roadways Monday.

senses.d: Characterized by coldness of manner; frigid; cold.
ex: I wasn't all the way icy. It wasn't like I could just give a girl a baby and forget about them.
Costello said the official visits were opportunities to pull Western allies closer, or to try to thaw icier relationships.

senses.d: To be wearing an excessive amount of jewelry, especially of the high-quality and expensive kind.
ex: Your bitch's a regular bitch, you're calling her wifey, I fucked her, I feed her fast food, you're keeping her icy.

grp.label: pertaining to, resembling, or abounding in ice
characterized by coldness, as of manner, influence, etc.

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Latin glaciālis. Morphologically, from glace + -ial.

Inherited from Latin gelātus, perfect passive participle of Latin gelō (“to freeze”). Cognate to Italian gelato. By surface analysis, helar (“to freeze, to cool”) + -ado (past participle suffix). Literally, “frozen.”
Learned borrowing from Latin gelidus (“cold”), from gelū (“frost; chill”).
